To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
CIITA is recurrently rearranged in lymphomas, that CIITA rearrangements impact tumour immune microenvironment interactions and that CIITA rearrangement impacts survival in PMBCL.
CIITA is recurrently fused to various partner genes in lymphoma and that these fusions result in downregulation of MHC class II and overexpression of CD274/PDL1, CD273/PDL1 and CIITA.
we have identified recurrent CIITA gene fusing partners in B cell lymphomas that are associated with decreased MHC class expression and increased expression of PD1 ligands.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of novel genetic alterations in lymphoid cancers and the characterization of their biological impact.
the molecular pathogenesis and immunobiology of lymphoid malignancies, with a particular focus on Hodgkin lymphoma and primary mediastinal large B cell lymphoma.
the identification of novel fusion transcripts resulting of translocations in Hodgkin lymphoma and primary mediastinal lymphoma cell lines.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CIITA gene fission may be a novel mechanism underlying tumor microenvironment connections across a spectrum of cancers.
CIITA gene fusing is a recurrent event in cHL, PMBCL and other lymphomas.
the CIITA rearrangements are a recurrent genetic event in PMBCL and cHL, and that these translocations result in the expression of novel fusion transcripts.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CIITA rearrangements are highly recurrent in lymphoid neoplasms, including classical Hodgkin lymphomas and primary mediastinal large B cell lymphomas.
we identified recurrent translocations involving CIITA in PMBCL and cHL.
we identified a recurrent gene fusion involving the gene CIITA in Hodgkin lymphoma and primary mediastinal lymphoma.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we found a novel recurrent gene fusion in Hodgkin lymphoma and in a subtype of B cell lymphoma called PMBCL.
CIITA is recurrently involved in chromosomal rearrangements in lymphoid cancers, and that CIITA gene fusing may have a role in shaping tumour immune interactions.
recurrent CIITA gene fusing events are highly prevalent in lymphoid cancers and that these gene fusions have a profound effect on the expression of MHC class II and its ligands PDL1 and PDL2.
